correctness.rationale: For all \(a,s>0\), \(m\geq1\), and \(q\geq m\), the companion Krylov space is exactly the first \(m\) coordinate axes. The \((m+1)\)-by-\(m\) least-squares matrix has full column rank and one-dimensional left kernel generated by \(w=(1,s^{-1},(1+as)s^{-2},\ldots,(1+as)s^{-m})\). Orthogonal projection gives \(R_m^2=1/W_m\). Recovery via the first block of \(L_0^{-1}\) yields signed physical residual \(r_0-ar_1=(1-a/s)/W_m\), and exact physical recovery occurs if and only if \(a=s\). Geometric-series evaluation proves every stated regime. An independent rational normal-equation implementation verifies 288 cases without treating finite checks as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact identity closes a meaningful distinction left open by a positive lifted residual floor: outside the unit parameter disk, first-step physically exact recovery can coexist with a permanently positive lifted residual, as shown by the parameter-matched resonance. Away from resonance and within the disk, physical error decays with twice the lifted residual exponent. This offers a sharp, reproducible test for interpreting lifted versus physical stopping criteria, without pretending scalar direct solves are computationally difficult.
